lines.quote: The prayers of good people got Donald Trump elected two weeks ago.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: This is a claim about why Trump won, not a reading of the war or the economy.

lines.quote: Wars with Russia and Iran are the counterattack.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It frames coming wars with Iran as retaliation, which reads as the no-war promise being broken.

lines.quote: Mark Levin was at the White House today, lobbying for war with Iran.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It names who is pushing for war, which is about blame and loyalties rather than the war's state.

lines.quote: there is zero credible intelligence that suggests Iran is anywhere near building a bomb
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It counters the case for war with counter-evidence, which supports staying out of war.

lines.quote: To distract you from the real goal, which is regime change
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It attributes hidden motives to the war's advocates, which is a blame story.

lines.quote: A war with Iran would amount to a profound betrayal of his supporters. It would end his presidency.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It says a war would break Trump's peace promise and bring political fallout.

lines.quote: The first week of a war with Iran could easily kill thousands of Americans.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It is a forecast of American deaths, and deaths are counted but never scored.

lines.quote: It could also collapse our economy, as surging oil prices trigger unmanageable inflation.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It gives a mechanism from war to oil prices to inflation.

lines.quote: An attack on Iran could very easily become a world war. We'd lose.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It says an attack would escalate into a wider war.

lines.quote: The real divide is between those who casually encourage violence, and those who seek to prevent it — between warmongers and peacemakers.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It is a story about camps and their loyalties, not a reading of the war.

lines.quote: anyone who's calling Donald Trump today to demand air strikes and other direct US military involvement
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It names people to blame for pushing US involvement.

lines.quote: how the president's enemies are working to destroy MAGA with the war on Iran
lines.subject: Steve Bannon, introduced by Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It says enemies are using the war against MAGA, which is a blame frame.

lines.quote: Senator Ted Cruz demands regime change in Iran.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It points to one senator's stated position, which is a speaker's record rather than the war itself.

lines.quote: Thank God.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It expresses relief at the June 24 end of fighting between Israel and Iran.

lines.quote: Thank God Trump brokered a ceasefire.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It reports a ceasefire after the US strikes, which the war rule scores at -0.5, though the speaker welcomes it.

lines.quote: That's the last thing Mark Levin wanted.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It speaks to what another man wanted, which is about motives and loyalties, not a reading.

lines.quote: Our interview with the president of Iran.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lit: interview with the president of Iran
lines.why: It announces an interview during the ceasefire and makes no claim about the state of the war.

lines.quote: This is Israel's last chance to blow up Iran with America's military
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It frames a coming US war on Iran as Israel's last chance to get one.

lines.quote: naturally the neocons have reached peak hysteria
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It blames a faction and describes its mood, which is attribution and not a reading.

lines.quote: So mightily spread abroad your Spirit, that all peoples may be gathered under the banner of the Prince of Peace
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson (quoting Newman)
lines.why: A prayer for peace posted as the war begins, a wish and not a reading of events.

lines.quote: Israel's war and what it means.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It labels the war as Israel's, which assigns ownership and blame and gives no reading.

lines.quote: Could this be a religious war designed to rebuild the Third Temple on the ashes of Al Aqsa?
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It frames the war now under way as possibly a religious war, which reads as the war frustrating the no-war promise.

lines.quote: how this war changes American politics forever
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson, introducing his guest Saagar Enjeti
lines.why: It frames the war as a lasting, transformative break in American politics, which reads as the object frustrated.

lines.quote: Pray that the spell breaks and the world is saved.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It casts the war as a spell that endangers the world, so it reads as strongly frustrated.

lines.quote: it should be illegal to yoke our military to a foreign power in war
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It proposes a ban on tying the US military to a foreign power, on the premise that the war does exactly that.

lines.quote: Bret Weinstein on how it happened.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson, introducing his guest Bret Weinstein
lines.why: It offers a story of how the US came to be yoked to a foreign power in the war.

lines.quote: why we actually went to war with Iran
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson, introducing his guest Joe Kent
lines.why: It treats the war as a fact with a hidden real cause, which reads as frustrated.

lines.quote: ground troops are often followed by tyranny in the country that sends them
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It argues that sending ground troops leads to tyranny at home, a warning against deepening the war.

lines.quote: We're spending more a year on the military in adjusted dollars than we did during World War II.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lit: than we did during World War II
lines.why: It states a spending record that implies heavy, wasteful war costs, which reads as frustrated.

lines.quote: how much is going to Israel?
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lit: How much is going to Israel
lines.why: It asks whose interests the spending serves, a question of loyalties that no instrument measures.

lines.quote: the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It forecasts a nuclear strike on Iran within days, which would be a major escalation of the war.

lines.quote: Netanyahu is cornered and desperate.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It puts the blame for the push toward war on Netanyahu's political survival and on allies inside the administration, not on a reading itself.

lines.quote: After eight months of conflict, Gulf economies are teetering. So are global energy and fertilizer markets.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It reports that the war has damaged energy markets, which maps most closely to the oil price.

lines.quote: In October alone, 11 of them were badly damaged in Hormuz. At this pace, a global depression is imminent.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It argues that tanker losses in Hormuz will tip the world economy into depression soon.

lines.quote: No one in Washington in either party seems bothered by this.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It says Congress has not used its power over the escalating war.

lines.quote: there is consensus there that more war is bad for everyone and a deal is worth making
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lit: more war is bad for everyone
a deal with Iran can be made
lines.why: It says a deal ending the war is still possible, though difficult.

lines.quote: Neocons and climate hysterics have at least one thing in common: they know nothing about energy.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It attacks the competence of neocons and climate advocates instead of reading any measured value.
